issues.description: The template declares the REST controller method getAllPersons() as public, while the solution declares the same handler method as private. This visibility difference is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected visibility of controller handler methods in PersonResource and about what must be implemented or preserved. It may also lead students to question whether Spring MVC handler methods must be public, causing uncertainty when implementing or testing endpoints.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Prefer declaring controller handler methods as public in both template and solution (change the solution's getAllPersons() to public) to match common Spring MVC expectations and the template. Alternatively, if private visibility is intentional, update the template and problem statement to explain and justify that handler methods may be non-public and ensure tests and examples reflect that design.
